LV vs optiland: stand-in-tabs (Stand-in tabs)

Each card is a tab of LensVisualizer, its heading the verdict of its identical rays (held to a limit) and of its own analysis beside its counterpart's (side by side). Choose the condition with the chips, and open a card's charts for the curves.

How to read this page

This page sets LensVisualizer's own analyses of this lens beside optiland's, a tab at a time, in one condition: a lens state of the lens, as the chips below choose it. Each card has two kinds of line. The identical rays: each engine traces the rays the tab launches, and the limits file holds every pair of engines to a limit. The tab's own analysis beside its counterpart's (optiland's, or for vignetting this tool's flux of LensVisualizer's rays): two methods set side by side with no limit, whose figures stand beside the review bands of the limits file at hand.

A side-by-side pair fails nothing: it is side by side where each figure with a review band is inside it, and worth a look where one is beyond it or the comparison set a field aside because the inputs differ. The comparison sorts every field or wavelength before any difference is taken: only one of two methods enters a figure, and the counts say how many it placed in each class (fields compared, of two methods; fields whose inputs differ, fields not converged, and fields an engine has no answer for, each set aside).

A condition is a lens state of the lens: its zoom and focus positions, its stop semi-diameter, its image plane (the MTF setup's kind of plane where a run has one, else the plane's position) and its wavelengths, as the lens state files state them. A chip keeps the facets before it, and a facet after it gives way to its first value where the lens state chosen so far has another.

A chip in grey is of lens states with no comparison of LensVisualizer beside a counterpart (a run directory of an older run, say): it is listed, and chosen only where it is asked.

Hover over a number to see the file it was read from and its JSON pointer there.

A number marked as derived is computed by the dashboard from the figures it names, never read from a file.

What each verdict means; the value stored in the files is shown on hover:

  • Pass: within limit (PASS): A check held to a limit: every judged figure is at or below its limit.
  • Within a known numerical floor (FLOOR): A check held to a limit: a judged figure is above its limit by a known numerical floor of one of the two engines, which a limits file may grant. It counts as a pass and is counted apart.
  • Fail: beyond limit (FAIL): A check held to a limit: a judged figure is above its limit, or is not a number.
  • Side by side (RECORDED): A side-by-side comparison with no limit: the difference is written down, inside its review band or with none. It is not a failure.
  • Side by side, worth a look (ATTENTION): A side-by-side comparison with no limit: a figure is outside its review band. It is not a failure.
  • Not computed (UNSUPPORTED): One of the two engines cannot compute what was asked. That is an answer, not a failure.
  • Not judged (an earlier check failed) (BLOCKED): The pair is not judged, whether or not both engines answered: an earlier check that this one rests on failed or ended in an error for the same two engines and the same lens state.
  • Error (ERROR): One of the two engines gave no result, or the two results cannot be compared.

Position: no zoom or focus position

Stop: stop semi-diameter 6.341241012139779 mm stop semi-diameter 5 mm stop semi-diameter 3 mm

Image plane: image plane at z 60 mm

Wavelengths: 2 wavelengths, 587.5618 to 537.5618 nm

The runs of this condition, each of the lens state shown: r10a-stand-ins: lens, r10b-stand-ins: lens, r9a-stand-ins: lens, r9b-stand-ins: lens, r11a-stand-ins: lens, r11b-stand-ins: lens, r12b-stand-ins: lens, r7a-stand-ins: lens, r8a-stand-ins: lens, r8b-stand-ins: lens

Lens stand-in-tabs

Run this lens

Run this lens starts lvrtc mtf as a job of run control, with the profile benchmark (the MTF tab), the profile tabs (LensVisualizer's other tabs) or both: the lens wide open and at the MTF tab's f/8 comparison, at the design plane and at LensVisualizer's best axial focus, at the reference wavelength and at the photopic spectrum's wavelengths, a zoom at both ends. It writes the run directories of the lens, mtf-<lensKey> and tabs-<lensKey>, which this page then gathers.

With real engines it is a heavy command: start it only when no other session runs one.

Engines are optional, ids of lv, reference-tracer, optiland separated by commas (lv alone when left empty); the aperture is one of wide-open, f/8, or both when left empty; the profile is one of benchmark, tabs, both, or benchmark when left empty; jobs is 1 to 4, and no more than the memory budget of this machine allows.
